title: Silence-Conditional Output Suppression for Training-Free Whisper Hallucination Mitigation

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to mitigate hallucinations in Whisper ASR on non-speech audio without requiring fine-tuning or external components. Paper [1] explicitly addresses the same problem of reducing hallucinations in Whisper ASR on non-speech audio, as stated in its title and abstract: "Reduce Whisper Hallucination On Non-Speech By Calming Crazy Heads Down." Paper [4] also focuses on mitigating hallucinations in Whisper ASR, though it emphasizes noisy acoustic conditions rather than non-speech audio specifically. However, [1] directly targets the same problem class (hallucinations on non-speech audio) and does so without external components, making it substantively equivalent in purpose.

### Mechanism
The mechanism, Silence-Conditional Output Suppression, uses Whisper's internal no-speech probability (`p_no_speech`) from the first decoder step to decide whether to output an empty transcription or proceed with decoding. None of the prior papers describe this specific mechanism. Paper [1] modifies Whisper's self-attentional heads to reduce hallucinations, which is a fundamentally different technical approach. Paper [4] uses adaptive layer attention and knowledge distillation, which also differs from leveraging the no-speech probability. While some papers (e.g., [19], [20], [22]) discuss reject option classification or abstention mechanisms, these are general frameworks and do not involve Whisper's internal no-speech probability or its specific application to hallucination mitigation. Thus, the mechanism is not covered.

### Evaluation
The evaluation reports a reduction in hallucination rate on UrbanSound8K, a benchmark dataset. Paper [1] also evaluates hallucination mitigation in Whisper ASR, though the specific dataset and metrics are not detailed in the excerpt. However, the evaluation design — measuring hallucination rates on a benchmark dataset — is a standard approach in ASR research and is not novel. Paper [4] also evaluates hallucination mitigation in Whisper ASR, likely using a similar design. Therefore, the evaluation design is covered.

### Domain
The domain is automatic speech recognition (ASR) with a focus on hallucination mitigation. Papers [1], [2], [4], and [7] all address hallucination issues in ASR, specifically in the context of Whisper. While the specific dataset (UrbanSound8K) and sub-problem (non-speech audio) are narrower, the general application area of ASR and hallucination mitigation is well-covered by prior work.
